lines.en: Pick on my shoulder, clinking as I walk.
The tunnel mouth is just ahead.
My boots slide on loose gravel.
I follow the quartz vein along.
My headlamp lights a small circle.
I have dug this tunnel half a year.
Dust falls down the back of my neck.
I feel along the wall in the dark.
Half a sack of slag on my back.
Three steps, two taps on the wall.
That blackstone ahead is stubborn.
I skirt the cracked ceiling.
I tap and listen to the echo.
This wall rings hollow when I knock.
The quartz glitters under my lamp.
Black dust fills my fingernails.
My pick tip needs replacing.
My lamp is half out of oil.
The gold ore is wedged in rock.
I count whether the props suffice.
Underground quiet is unsettling.
I sit a while at the tunnel mouth.
You are standing on my map.
What brings a stranger down this shaft?
Do not touch my support beams.
Quartz dust is on your soles.
Buying ore? Look at the goods.
Your lamp is far too bright.
This level is mine to work.
You carry no dust on you at all.
Do not stand under the crack.
Your hands look like they never dug.
My helmet took part of it.
I lean on the wall and stay up.

lines.zh: 顶上落下来的灰更多了。
lines.en: More dust falls from the roof.
The blow set my tusks ringing.
My lamp is still burning.
The smell of blood lingers here.
I check; nothing is broken.
Do not mind me; watch the ceiling.
I grip the pick even tighter.
I will deal with this wound at home.
That quartz is good grade.
Gold ore? I know it at a glance.
Give me a decent pick instead.
Lamp oil matters more than gold.
This rock rings when it is tapped.
No trade; my face is unfinished.
The rope you carry I could use.
Gold is heavy; let me weigh it.
I know that ore; it is worthless.
Good ore goes to those who know it.
My lamp nearly fell.
The bump shook dust from above.
You stepped on my pick handle.
This tunnel is too narrow.
My basket swayed once.
Step aside; I carry rock.
You knocked my helmet crooked.
Steady; the floor is all gravel.
We are jammed at the corner.
Do not push; the roof may fall.
She complains about my dust.
A home means digging a stone room.
She sewed me an ore pouch.

lines.zh: 我在攒一块好石英送她。
lines.en: I am saving good quartz for her.
Two digging in shifts go faster.
The little ones must stay out of shafts.
I am tongue-tied; I give stones.
The wedding table should be gold.
She says earn gold, then marry.
I carved her name on a prop.
A piece of quartz; usable.
Whose gold nugget fell here?
This rope can still tie a basket.
I flip the stone over to look.
A blackstone block to prop my feet.
The lamp wick fell to the floor.
There is still some left in this slag.
Picking up gold is a habit I cannot break.
Too much dust; it slipped from me.
This nail is just what I needed.
Footsteps echo through the shaft.
Its shadow covers my lamp.
Who pulled down my support beam?
Dust is starting to fall from above.
It blocks the only way out.
I settle the pick in my main hand.
This one is not here to buy ore.
I knock the wall to signal above.
It crushed the quartz vein.
I step back deeper into the shaft.
My lamp cannot reach it.
Someone follows my cart tracks.
Stay back; this part will collapse.
I guard this lamp first.
I hug the wall and follow it.
Its breathing bounces off the rock.
I turn my lamp down lower.
It slips into a side branch.
I know every branch down here.
It crushed the marker I set.
I crouch and listen through the rock.
It is ten paces behind me.
I circle back to cut it off.
Keep it away from the props.
I raise the pick beside my shoulder.
It hunts an exit; so do I.
The light sweeps forward an inch.
I know this depth better than it.
The pick point cracks its shoulder.
That swing came with a crunch.
I smash down by its feet.
Rock chips fly over both of us.
It backs up; I follow with the pick.
I block across with the haft.
I missed and hit a support beam.
Its claw scraped across my arm guard.
I swing the lamp at its face.
My hand shook; the pick nearly flew.
Years of breaking stone built this.
I retreat under the timber frame.
It has grabbed my ore sack.
After this I must shore the roof.
I light my lamp and head down.
Today I reach the quartz layer.
The shaft is bitterly cold at night.
Pick on shoulder; I set out.
Yesterday's hole still needs filling.
Dust settles on the tip of my snout.
This new tunnel is barely started.
I brought two flasks of lamp oil.
The tunnel mouth is warmer than inside.
I check every support beam.
The village waits for my ore.
I walk in along the old cart rails.
Lava seeps out of the rock seam.
I fell off the shaft scaffold.
The shaft is flooding; bad.
Was that gas or a charge?
The arrow came from deep inside.
The lamp flame turned green.
I have stayed underground too long.
Thunder rolls down the shaft.
I fell into an abandoned shaft.
